stem: A postpartum client develops heavy bleeding with signs of hypovolemia. The nurse recognizes postpartum hemorrhage and the facility has an established obstetric hemorrhage response protocol. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Activate the standardized hemorrhage protocol promptly so the interprofessional team can begin the predefined assessment, resuscitation, treatment, and escalation process without waiting for deterioration.
options.B: Wait for the attending clinician to arrive before initiating the facility’s hemorrhage response because nurses should not activate standardized emergency protocols.
options.C: Use the hemorrhage protocol only after cesarean birth because standardized postpartum hemorrhage response does not apply after vaginal delivery.
options.D: Delay protocol activation until the exact cause of bleeding is fully confirmed because coordinated response should begin only after a definitive diagnosis.

rationale: A is correct. ACOG’s postpartum hemorrhage guidance emphasizes rapid recognition, evaluation, treatment, and implementation of standardized hemorrhage bundles, policies, guidelines, and algorithms to support coordinated obstetric care. A client with heavy postpartum bleeding and hypovolemic signs should therefore trigger the facility’s established response promptly while evaluation of the cause continues. B creates an unsafe delay in a time-sensitive emergency. C is false because postpartum hemorrhage can occur after any birth route. D is incorrect because stabilization and coordinated response should not be postponed until every etiologic detail is known.
educational_objective: Activate an established obstetric hemorrhage protocol promptly when postpartum hemorrhage is recognized so assessment, resuscitation, treatment, and escalation occur in a coordinated manner while the cause is evaluated.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
source_version_date: Practice Bulletin reaffirmed 2024; July 2025 Clinical Practice Update; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Practice Bulletin abstract and purpose — postpartum hemorrhage requires evaluation, prevention, and management; obstetric care providers should implement standardized bundles of care, including policies, guidelines, and algorithms, for postpartum hemorrhage management; bulletin includes acute medical management framework
source_claim_supported: ACOG supports standardized obstetric hemorrhage bundles/protocols to enable prompt, coordinated evaluation and management of postpartum hemorrhage rather than delaying response until deterioration or complete etiologic confirmation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; initiate emergency response systems, coordinate interprofessional care, and implement established protocols for rapidly changing client conditions
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — activation of a standardized postpartum hemorrhage response protocol
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source descriptive protocol item into a time-sensitive nursing coordination decision and corrected the category from Safety and Infection Prevention and Control to Management of Care. The final version stays at the level supported by ACOG—prompt standardized bundle/protocol activation—without inventing one universal set of staff roles or stage thresholds for all institutions.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: postpartum hemorrhage / emergency protocol / interprofessional coordination
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against the ACOG Postpartum Hemorrhage Practice Bulletin, reaffirmed 2024 with a July 2025 update. Its stated purpose includes implementation of standardized bundles, policies, guidelines, and algorithms for hemorrhage management.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A requires prompt activation of an existing facility protocol while etiology is evaluated; it does not prescribe a specific institutional stage, medication sequence, transfusion ratio, or team composition not present in the accessible source.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; standardized response should begin promptly in recognized postpartum hemorrhage.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; waiting for bedside arrival of one clinician can delay an established emergency response.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; postpartum hemorrhage is not limited to cesarean birth.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; emergency stabilization and coordinated management proceed while the cause is being identified.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A balances rapid protocol activation with ongoing cause assessment and stays within nursing emergency-response responsibilities.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are protocol-activation decisions in the same hemorrhage scenario.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is the best fit because the nurse activates a standardized emergency system and coordinates interprofessional care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked ACOG currentness, standardized-bundle claim, protocol activation versus independent prescribing, birth-route scope, cause-identification timing, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
